title: Why the dollar follows interest rates
hook: What decides whether the dollar goes up or down against other money?
metaphor: Two piggy banks sit side by side. One pays 5% a year, one pays 1%. Where would you put a billion dollars?
body: Big money parks where safe savings pay the most.
To park money in America, you must first buy dollars.
So when US rates rise faster than elsewhere, the dollar usually rises.
Most currency moves are this one comparison, repeated all day.

caveat: Rate gaps explain most currency moves, not all. Trade flows and panics can override them for months.
